claim_zh: Higher inflation level at FIRST_HIKE was associated with worse subsequent Gold in this sample; this contradicts a simple high-inflation-is-bullish rule.
evidence_text: HIGH median Gold 12M -11.8% vs LOW_OR_MODERATE +6.5%; diff -18.3%.
boundary: Event-level descriptive association; macro values are current-vintage/release-lag aware, not strict ALFRED PIT.

claim_zh: Inflation direction and inflation level are different states: rising inflation was associated with better Gold than falling/flat even though HIGH inflation level was associated with worse Gold.
evidence_text: RISING median Gold 12M +3.1% vs FALLING_OR_FLAT -11.8%; diff +14.8%.
boundary: Descriptive heterogeneity, not a causal inflation beta.

claim_zh: Weak-growth FIRST_HIKE states were associated with somewhat stronger Gold outcomes than strong-growth states.
evidence_text: STRONG median Gold 12M -3.5% vs WEAK +4.8%; diff -8.3%.
boundary: Small historical event set; no recession forecast.

claim_zh: Rising energy was associated with better subsequent Gold in the supported event contrast.
evidence_text: RISING energy median Gold 12M +3.6% vs FALLING_OR_FLAT -2.6%; diff +6.2%.
boundary: Energy direction is not identified as the causal driver.

claim_zh: The event-level USD diagnostic is counterintuitive relative to the common inverse-USD story and is retained as evidence of confounding/era dependence rather than deleted.
evidence_text: USD RISING median Gold 12M +3.6% vs FALLING_OR_FLAT -11.8%; diff +15.4%.
boundary: USD bridge diagnostic; not promoted to primary mechanism evidence.

claim_zh: USD remains a mechanism candidate but the positive sign does not survive secondary-family multiplicity control and should not be called a confirmed driver.
evidence_text: Within-cycle beta per 1SD = +0.0183 Gold forward-6M return; broad exact p=0.03125; LOO sign stable=True.
boundary: Hypothesis-generating secondary diagnostic; source-era restrictions reduce precision.

claim_zh: This public design does not establish the textbook inverse real-rate/Gold relation; the proxy estimate is positive and statistically weak in this secondary diagnostic.
evidence_text: Within-cycle beta per 1SD = +0.0180; broad exact p=0.26562; LOO sign stable=True.
boundary: Proxy-based association, not a real-yield causal estimate.

claim_zh: Actual 10Y TIPS real-yield history is too short in this Fed-cycle design to support a stable Gold mechanism claim.
boundary: Do not infer absence of a global real-yield relationship; this design is under-supported.

claim_zh: NFCI does not show a stable Gold forward-return association in the monthly secondary diagnostic.
evidence_text: Within-cycle beta per 1SD = -0.0067; broad exact p=0.59375; LOO sign stable=False.
boundary: No signal claim; financial stress may matter conditionally through other channels.

claim_zh: Gold often reaches its trough before credit-stress maxima rather than waiting for the stress peak.
evidence_text: Gold trough median M5 vs Baa stress peak M7; lead median -3m; near-2m share 14.3%.
boundary: Ex-post timing description; not a real-time Gold-entry rule.

claim_zh: Gold timing differs from U.S. equities: its trough can precede later VIX stress maxima by several months.
evidence_text: Gold trough median M4 vs VIX stress peak M8; lead median -4m; near-2m share 40.0%.
boundary: Supports timing heterogeneity, not a safe-haven timing signal.

claim_zh: Copper/Gold timing is closer in the supported sample than Baa/VIX timing, but still cannot be used as a deterministic signal.
evidence_text: Gold trough median M4 vs copper stress peak M9; median lead +0m; near-2m share 60.0%.

claim_zh: Defines hedge as average non/negative correlation and safe haven as non/negative correlation in market stress; reports Gold safe-haven behavior in extreme stock conditions and notes the effect can be short-lived.
evidence_text: Is Gold a Hedge or a Safe Haven? An Analysis of Stocks, Bonds and Gold
boundary: External literature context; does not overwrite repository evidence.

claim_zh: Finds hedge/safe-haven properties differ across developed and emerging markets, so safe-haven behavior is not universal across countries.
evidence_text: Is gold a safe haven? International evidence
boundary: External literature context; does not overwrite repository evidence.

claim_zh: Argues Gold is an unreliable inflation hedge over practical investment horizons even if very long-run purchasing-power arguments can differ.
boundary: External literature context; does not overwrite repository evidence.

claim_zh: Shows commonly attributed Gold properties can change between simple and multiple-regression settings; highlights USD and commodity-price channels.
evidence_text: Explanatory mining for gold: Contrasting evidence from simple and multiple regressions
boundary: External literature context; does not overwrite repository evidence.

claim_zh: Reports a regime-dependent real-rate/Gold relationship and a positive association in its G7 MS-VECM results, illustrating that the sign need not be universally inverse.
evidence_text: Do gold prices respond to real interest rates? Evidence from the Bayesian Markov Switching VECM model
boundary: External literature context; does not overwrite repository evidence.
